claims.text: Thermomechanical processing can induce nanoscale coherent carbide or nitride precipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy matrix.
The proposed thermomechanical processing may consist of cold rolling followed by aging.
The induced nanoscale coherent precipitates will be distributed within the alloy matrix.
The coherent precipitates will act as dislocation sources.
The coherent precipitates will act as obstacles to dislocation motion or pile-up.
The precipitates will facilitate dislocation movement and thereby enhance ductility.
The precipitates will increase strain hardening and preserve high strength by obstructing dislocations.
Maintaining precipitate coherence and nanoscale size will prevent embrittlement.
Maintaining precipitate coherence and nanoscale size will preserve the alloy's impact-induced energetic response.
The intervention will increase uniform elongation by at least 20% relative to the untreated baseline.
The intervention will improve overall ductility by at least 20% relative to the untreated baseline.
The processed alloy's yield strength will remain within 10% of the untreated baseline value.
The processed alloy's impact-induced energy release will remain within 10% of the untreated baseline value.
The predicted benefits should hold from room temperature to approximately 800°C.
The predicted benefits should hold under both quasi-static and dynamic loading relevant to energetic structural applications.
Precipitate fractions above approximately 5 vol% may cause embrittlement.
Loss of precipitate coherence may cause embrittlement.
Excessive precipitate fraction or loss of coherence may reduce impact-induced energetic response.
The effect on impact-induced energy release may depend on precipitate chemistry and spatial distribution.
There is a lack of direct prior evidence for the proposed ductility and uniform-deformability improvement.
